scientists: people who study or work in fields of science

still: continuing to be the case; even more so

debate: a formal or informal discussion in which people argue different views
The debate over the new tax law lasted for hours in parliament.
useful: able to be used effectively for a purpose; helpful

long: having a great length or duration

run: to move quickly, or to continue moving under its own momentum

same: They wore the same colour shirts to the reunion.

poison: a substance that can kill or harm if swallowed or absorbed

source: the place or thing from which something originates
The river's source is a spring high in the mountains.
slice: a thin, flat piece cut from something larger

birthday: the anniversary of the day someone was born
They threw a small party to celebrate her tenth birthday.
cake: a sweet baked food made from flour, sugar and eggs
She baked a chocolate cake for her son's birthday party.
crisis: a time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger
The company faced a financial crisis after losing its biggest client.
problem: a matter that is difficult to deal with or solve
The main problem with the plan was its enormous cost.
quiet: making little or no noise; calm
The library is usually quiet enough for deep concentration.
total: the whole amount of something added together

regularly: often, at even and predictable intervals
She visits her grandmother regularly, usually every Sunday afternoon.
far: to a great extent; at or to a great distance

recommended: suggested that something was good or advisable

linked: có liên quan đến, được nối

gain: an increase or benefit obtained from something

tooth: one of the hard white structures in the mouth used for biting

decay: the gradual process of rotting, breaking down, or declining

sugary: containing a lot of sugar; tasting very sweet
Sugary drinks are often blamed for rising rates of tooth decay.
associated: connected or linked with something else

higher: greater in height or degree; comparative of high
Prices are noticeably higher near the tourist areas.
risk: the possibility of something bad or dangerous happening
Investing in a new business always carries some risk.
type: a category of people or things sharing common characteristics

diabetes: a disease in which the body cannot properly control blood sugar levels
Regular exercise can help lower the risk of type 2 diabetes.
news: She checks the news on her phone first thing every morning.
change: A single ingredient can change the whole flavour of a dish.
down: toward a lower position or level
Please sit down and make yourself comfortable.
step: one action in a series, or a single movement of the foot
Booking the flight was the first step in planning the trip.
after: following in time or place; later than
The shop stays open late after the holiday season begins.
weeks: Within weeks, algae settle on the new surface underwater.
seem: to give the impression of being something
The instructions seem confusing at first glance.
shops: places where goods are sold to the public
Small shops line the narrow streets of the old town.
already: before now or before a particular time
By the time we arrived, the meeting had already started.
let: to allow someone to do something
Her parents let her stay out late for the concert.
customers: people who buy goods or services from a business
The café attracts customers with its freshly roasted coffee.
choose: to select one thing from a number of possibilities
Students can choose between three different elective subjects.
half: one of two equal parts of something
She gave half of the sandwich to her brother.
usual: happening or done most of the time; typical
Its usual destination was the robe of the most important figure in the painting.
governments: groups of people with authority to govern countries

tax: money that people must pay to the government

hoping: wishing or expecting something to happen
We are hoping for good weather during the festival.
companies: businesses that make or sell goods or provide services
Several companies competed to win the government construction contract.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
personal: belonging to or affecting a particular individual rather than others
He kept a personal diary to record his thoughts each evening.
habits: things done regularly, almost without thinking
Good sleeping habits make a noticeable difference to concentration.
public: provided by the state for everyone; open to all people
The new library is open to the public every day of the week.
rules: official instructions stating what may or may not be done
New traffic rules were introduced to reduce accidents.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
together: with each other; combined into one group or place

most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of

habit: a thing done regularly, almost without thinking

curiosity: a strong desire to know or learn something
điều tò mò, tính tò mò

turning: moving or rotating in a circular direction

over: during the whole of a period of time; more than

takes: gets hold of, requires, or needs an amount of time or effort

seconds: units of time, sixty of which make a minute
The whole process took only a few seconds to complete.
familiar: The song sounded familiar, though she couldn't remember its name.
story: an account of events, real or imagined, told for interest
She wrote a short story about her grandmother's village.
right: correct or suitable for a particular situation
Choosing the right moment to speak up can be difficult.
give: to hand over or provide something to someone
Please give the documents to the manager before noon.
just: I just finished reading the report you sent this morning.
noticed: became aware of something; saw or observed something
He noticed a small crack in the wall near the window.
someone: Someone called while you were out this afternoon.
else: in addition to, or other than, someone or something already mentioned
Ask someone else if you need a second opinion on this.
